title: UN talks on limits for autonomous weapons

charter.in: Intergovernmental talks at the UN on limiting lethal autonomous weapons systems (weapons that select and attack targets without human input). This covers the Group of Governmental Experts under the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva, the push to open binding treaty negotiations at the CCW review meeting of 16-20 November 2026, and the UN, ICRC and civil-society appeals aimed at those talks. Covered from August 2026.
out: Battlefield use and development of autonomous drones (Russia, Ukraine), including the Zaporizhzhia strike itself
National military AI adoption, targeting tools and procurement (US Maven, Pentagon AI deals, Israeli targeting in Gaza, US autonomous fighter drones)
Chinese military AI and autonomous-weapon prototypes
A US-China human-in-the-loop understanding on nuclear weapons
UN Security Council briefings on frontier-AI risk
The UN's military-AI forum and voluntary company guidelines
Nuclear arms control talks (non-proliferation review, New START)
charter.endEvent: States adopt a legally binding instrument limiting autonomous weapons (a new CCW protocol or a stand-alone treaty), or formally abandon the effort. The November 2026 review meeting's decision on whether to open negotiations is a turning point, not the end.

notes: Not closed. On 16 Nov the Geneva review meeting is 'only deciding whether to begin negotiations', and the US-Russian opposition is reported as 'expected', a forecast, not a decision. So 16 Nov is neither the end nor a breakdown; the meeting's outcome (mandate adopted or blocked) will be the next turning point. Under this charter the development ends only with a binding instrument or the formal abandonment of the effort. The 6 Sep and 8 Sep stories report the same end of the expert-group session: 6 Sep (RFI) gives the 128-state consensus on a definition and human control and is the turning point; 8 Sep (HRW) adds that the report was 'watered-down' by US and Russian interventions and that 76 states back binding talks, so it is routine. Our 26 Aug and 6 Sep stories, from RFI's French, call the convention 'CCAC'. 26 Aug names the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons in the same text, so it is the CCW. Figures are []: 76 states backing binding talks appears only on 8 Sep. '128' appears twice with different meanings (states in the expert-group consensus on 6 Sep; countries at the Geneva meeting on 16 Nov). The 13 Nov story's archive title is 'Rights groups urge treaty talks on autonomous weapons'; its slug still reads 'states-urged-to-negotiate-limits-on-weapons-that-choose-targets'. The 3 Sep story ties the appeal to the Russian drone strike: appeals that cite battlefield cases belong, and the battlefield stories themselves stay out.
